units.source_text: [\[20\]](#part1334.html#w20) 昔日日本儿童习字之初，必书《难波津之歌》。

en.t: [20] In former times, when Japanese children first began learning to write, they always copied The Song of Naniwazu.

units.source_text: 歌云：“辽阔难波津，寂寞冬眠花；和煦阳春玉，香艳满枝枒。”

en.t: The song says: "In broad Naniwazu, the flowers sleep lonely through winter; when the gentle spring sun comes, their fragrance and beauty fill every branch."

units.source_text: 难波津是古地名，今大阪。

en.t: Naniwazu is an old place name, referring to present-day Osaka.
